purpose: Canonical short-form glossary definitions for inline teaching and the SOUBEL A-Z Knowledge Library.

records.definition: An electrode that supplies protective current to the structure in a cathodic-protection system.
A power unit that converts AC electricity to controlled DC output for an impressed-current cathodic-protection system.
A stable electrical reference used to compare the potential of the protected structure.
An aboveground access point that brings selected electrical leads from a buried or submerged structure to a location where technicians can make measurements, inspect connections, or evaluate bonds.
A small metal sample electrically connected to or associated with a structure and used to help evaluate localized cathodic-protection conditions.
An enclosure used to organize electrical leads, bonds, resistors, shunts, and monitoring connections in a cathodic-protection system.
A device that collects selected field measurements and transmits them for off-site review.
A device that detects or measures a selected physical or electrical condition and provides data for monitoring or evaluation.
The conductors, splices, terminations, and related connections that carry current or measurement signals between parts of the cathodic-protection system.
A continuous conductive path that allows electrical current to flow through connected parts of the structure.
Electrical influence from another current source that changes the conditions on the structure being protected.
The voltage difference measured between a metallic structure and a reference electrode in the surrounding electrolyte.
Close-interval potential survey / close-interval survey: closely spaced structure-to-electrolyte potential readings collected along a buried pipeline.
Direct current voltage gradient: an aboveground survey method used to help locate coating defects and evaluate current flow around a buried pipeline.
External corrosion direct assessment: a structured process that combines pre-assessment, indirect inspection, direct examination, and post-assessment to evaluate external corrosion threats.
